sections.skill: Choose a level of accuracy for very large and very small quantities

questions.skill: Choose a level of accuracy for very large and very small quantities
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Earth's mean radius is about 6,371 km. Write it to one significant digit as a single digit times a power of 10.
questions.prompt_markup:
Earth's mean radius is about 6,371 km.
Write it to one significant digit as a single digit times a power of 10.

questions.skill: Choose a level of accuracy for very large and very small quantities
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A scale reads to the nearest 0.1 kg. One bag of rice measures 2.3 kg, and a truck carries 4,000 such bags. Report the total mass in scientific notation, with no more accuracy than the scale supports.
questions.prompt_markup:
A scale reads to the nearest 0.1 kg. One bag of rice measures 2.3 kg, and a truck carries 4,000 such bags.
Report the total mass in scientific notation, with no more accuracy than the scale supports.
questions.grading_note: 9.2 × 10³ kg (two significant digits). Reports such as 9.200 × 10³ kg claim more accuracy than the scale gives.

questions.skill: Choose a level of accuracy for very large and very small quantities
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A runner's time over 100 m was measured to the nearest second as 12 s. A calculator gives 100 ÷ 12 = 8.333333. Which report of the speed fits the accuracy of the measurement?
questions.prompt_markup:

questions.skill: Choose a level of accuracy for very large and very small quantities
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)

questions.grading_note: Writing more digits does not make an estimate more accurate.

sections.skill: Use base-10 logarithms to solve exponential equations

questions.skill: Use base-10 logarithms to solve exponential equations
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A bacteria count is 10^t thousand after t hours. Use a logarithm to find when the count reaches 1,000,000 (1,000 thousand).
questions.prompt_markup:
A bacteria count is 10^t thousand after t hours.
Use a logarithm to find when the count reaches 1,000,000 (1,000 thousand).

questions.skill: Use base-10 logarithms to solve exponential equations
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Solve 5 · 10^x = 2,000. Write x as a logarithm, then use a calculator to round it to the nearest tenth.
questions.prompt_markup: Solve 5 · 10^x = 2,000. Write x as a logarithm, then use a calculator to round it to the nearest tenth.
questions.grading_note: Both the logarithm and the rounded value are required.
